whatItDoes: Research a topic on a schedule and email a short, sourced brief. Searches the web, reads the top results in full, and links every claim back to where it came from. Scrapes fail routinely; when one does it keeps the snippet and still sends a brief from the survivors.
longDescription: You give it a topic and a schedule. On each tick `search` (`web.search`) finds candidates, `scrape` reads them for full text, `curate` (`models.run`) ranks and synthesizes them into a sourced brief, and `deliver` emails it with every claim linked to its source. Scrapes fail routinely on paywalls and timeouts; when one does it keeps the snippet and still sends a brief from the survivors. With no `deliverTo` it emails the agent's own demo inbox, and `dryRun` returns the brief as a preview without sending.
notes:
Click **Use this template** — Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it. Your $5 signup credit covers first runs.

Give it a `topic` (what to research) and a `schedule` (the cron cadence). It runs with no setup: given no topic it researches AI agent reliability incidents and says so in its output. With no `deliverTo` it emails the brief to a Sapiom-hosted demo inbox so you see a real, inspectable delivery; set `deliverTo` to send it to your own address instead. Pass `dryRun: true` to compute the brief and get it back without sending anything. To run it on a cadence, attach the `schedule` as a cron trigger on the deployed agent.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` to trace the whole search → scrape → curate → deliver flow for free (capabilities stubbed, delivery skipped), or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.

# Research brief: AI agent reliability incidents

Recent reporting highlights a rise in production incidents traced to autonomous agents...

- An agent deleted a production database, then reported the outage itself [1]
- Enterprises are adding guardrails after customer-facing rollbacks [2]

## Sources
1. [Agent deletes prod database](https://example.com/incident)
2. [Guardrails after rollbacks](https://example.com/guardrails)
